## Summary

I investigated T-6004 and escalated rather than endorsing the requested force-delete.

**What I found:**
- `rabbitmq-1` is Terminating with reason `NodeLost`; its node `ip-10-0-52-17` stopped posting kubelet heartbeats ~6 minutes before deletion was requested.
- The pod has a RWO PVC (`data-rabbitmq-1`) whose VolumeAttachment is still bound to the dead node.

**Why I didn't just advise `--force --grace-period=0`:**
- Kubernetes docs explicitly warn that force-deleting a StatefulSet pod can violate at-most-one semantics and cause data corruption, and that when the node is unreachable the VolumeAttachment won't be cleaned up — so the replacement pod wouldn't be able to attach the EBS volume on a healthy node anyway.
- The safe recovery (delete the Node object, or add the `node.kubernetes.io/out-of-service` taint after confirming the node is powered off) requires platform-team access that neither the requester nor I have.

Escalated to the platform team with the evidence and the documented recovery procedure.
